text: Tests often need the same setup — some data, a database, a file — and fixtures provide it cleanly.
A fixture is a function marked with the fixture decorator that returns whatever your tests need.
Here sample_users hands back a ready-made list of user dictionaries.
[chuckle] Any test can request it just by naming it as a parameter — pytest injects the value automatically.
So both tests receive the same fresh data, without repeating the setup code in each one.
[sniff] Fixtures can also handle teardown — cleanup that runs after the test, no matter what.
The yield splits it: everything before prepares, the test runs at the yield, and everything after cleans up.
[sigh] pytest even ships built-in fixtures like tmp_path, giving each test its own temporary folder.
[groan] Fixtures keep your tests dry and focused — set up once, reuse everywhere, and clean up reliably.
